faqs.a: It removes comments, indentation and redundant whitespace, and drops the final semicolon before a CSS closing brace. It does not rename variables or restructure code, so savings of 15-40% are typical for human-written code, less for already-compact code.
faqs.q: How much smaller do files get?

faqs.q: Does minification change what my code does?

faqs.a: Because the minifier masks them before touching anything else. Strings, template literals and regex literals are extracted first, the code is shrunk, then they are restored byte for byte. A // inside a URL string is never mistaken for a comment.
faqs.q: Why are my strings never broken?

code-minifier.formula:
JavaScript: tokenize (strings, template literals, regex, comments masked) -> drop comments (replaced by a newline, ASI-safe) -> collapse horizontal whitespace -> strip spaces around { } ( ) ; , : [ ] -> drop newlines only around safe punctuation, never between operands.
CSS: drop comments -> collapse whitespace -> strip spaces around { } : ; , and inside ( ) -> drop the last ; before }.
HTML: extract pre/textarea/script/style raw -> drop comments -> collapse whitespace between tags -> collapse remaining runs to one space.
howTo: Pick the language tab: JavaScript, CSS or HTML.

For production bundles, prefer Terser or esbuild; this tool is for quick, safe shrinking.
keyFacts: A lightweight minifier for JavaScript, CSS and HTML that removes comments and redundant whitespace.
String-aware tokenizing: quotes, template literals and regex literals are masked before shrinking and restored untouched.
JavaScript: comments become newlines (never empty deletions), so ASI behaviour is preserved; newlines are dropped only around safe punctuation.
CSS: spaces stripped around braces, colons, semicolons and commas; the final semicolon before } is dropped; @media and (...) spacing stays valid.
HTML: comments removed, whitespace between tags collapsed; pre, textarea, script and style contents are kept byte-for-byte.
Minification is live: every keystroke re-minifies instantly, entirely in your browser.
